title: High-Resolution Image Synthesis with Latent Diffusion (Stable Diffusion)
hook: Running diffusion on raw pixels is brutally expensive. Do it in a compressed latent space instead, and high-res text-to-image becomes cheap enough to run on a consumer GPU.
key_points: Runs the diffusion process in a compressed latent space from an autoencoder, not on raw pixels.
Drastically cuts the compute needed for high-resolution image generation.
Adds text and other conditioning via cross-attention in the denoising network.
Open-sourced as Stable Diffusion, putting text-to-image in many hands.
Helped launch the consumer text-to-image wave.
content_html: Rombach, Blattmann, and colleagues made high-resolution diffusion practical by moving the expensive denoising work out of pixel space and into a compact latent space learned by an autoencoder. The same team open-sourced the approach as Stable Diffusion, which put capable text-to-image generation into the hands of ordinary users.
extra_html:
How it works

First, an autoencoder learns to compress images into a much smaller latent representation and decode them back with little visible loss. The diffusion model then does all its noising and denoising on these latents rather than on full-resolution pixels, which is far cheaper because the data is so much smaller. To condition on a text prompt, the denoising network uses cross-attention, letting each step attend to the prompt's encoded meaning. A final decode step turns the cleaned-up latent back into a full image.

Why it matters

By slashing the compute cost of diffusion, latent diffusion made high-quality image generation runnable on widely available hardware instead of large clusters. Released openly as Stable Diffusion, it triggered an explosion of consumer text-to-image apps, fine-tunes, and creative tools, and its latent-space approach influenced later generative systems well beyond images.

related.hook: Wreck an image into pure static one tiny step at a time, then train a network to undo it. Run the undo from random noise and you get a brand-new image.

related.hook: Skip the fixed label list. Train on image–caption pairs so pictures and text share one space, and you can classify images from plain-text labels you make up on the spot.

related.hook: Don't just compress data to a point — compress it to a distribution. That gives a smooth latent space you can sample from to generate genuinely new data.

flashcards.prompt: Why is latent diffusion far cheaper than pixel-space diffusion?

choices.text: It runs noising and denoising on a small autoencoder latent, not full-resolution pixels
It uses fewer denoising steps than DDPM
It skips the decoding step entirely

flashcards.explanation_html: An autoencoder compresses images into a much smaller latent; diffusion operates there, so the data being processed is far smaller.

flashcards.prompt: How does latent diffusion condition generation on a text prompt?
flashcards.back_html: The denoising network uses cross-attention, letting each step attend to the prompt's encoded meaning.

flashcards.prompt: What was the broader impact of open-sourcing this as Stable Diffusion?
flashcards.back_html: It made high-quality image generation runnable on widely available hardware, triggering an explosion of consumer text-to-image apps and fine-tunes.
